plans.note: Primary review at sec-21 (Limitation of Liability): check mutuality, cap quantum/multiple of Fees, exclusion of indirect damages, and the carve-out set. Cross-check the 'Excluded Claims' definition in sec-1 and the indemnity in sec-20, since carve-outs are likely defined there rather than restated in sec-21.

Section 20 is the indemnification clause; confirm Vendor IP infringement indemnity plus misconduct/data breach coverage, defence and control mechanics, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow. Cross-reference sec-14 (IP/Deliverables) for infringement remedies and sec-21 for whether the indemnity is carved out of the cap.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant heading. Sweep sec-30 (General) and sec-12 (Customer Responsibilities) for any covenant limiting the businesses we operate or competing products we may buy or build; expect none.

Check sec-2 (Agreement Structure and Scope) and sec-4 (Order Forms/Affiliate Orders) for sole-source or 'all requirements' language binding Customer, and sec-12 for any obligation to route work through Vendor; likely no exclusivity in this structure.
Look in sec-7 (Fees/Invoicing) for pricing-parity or best-terms language. Only flag if the MFN runs against us; an MFN in Customer's favour is welcome and should not be redlined.

No standalone heading; non-solicits are commonly buried in sec-30 (General) or attached to personnel/confidentiality provisions (sec-12, sec-16). Test duration, scope (Vendor personnel actually engaged), mutuality, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 9 (Termination) is primary: confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without early-termination fees, and that Vendor has no matching convenience right mid-term. Check sec-8 for term interaction and sec-10/sec-7 for any termination charges or non-refundable prepaid Fees.

Section 8 (Term and Renewal): assess auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window measured against our preferred maximum, and any renewal price uplift cap in sec-8 or sec-7. A missing uplift cap alone is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Section 28 covers governing law and dispute resolution. Confirm the law is New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seated arbitration; an accepted-but-not-preferred law is a note only.

Section 24 (Assignment and Change of Control): confirm Customer may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that Vendor has no right to terminate or reprice on our change of control. Check sec-30 for any residual assignment boilerplate.

Section 14 governs ownership of Deliverables and Vendor Technology; sec-15 governs Customer Data. Confirm Customer owns paid-for Deliverables and all Customer Data, that no Customer IP or data is assigned or licensed broadly to Vendor, and check any Vendor 'improvements'/feedback or aggregated-data grab in sec-14/sec-15 and the sec-1 definitions.

Section 13 (Access Rights and Licence): test whether the grant extends to our Affiliates and contractors/service providers acting on our behalf, and that it is not revocable at will or suspendable outside genuine breach. Cross-check sec-4 for Affiliate ordering and sec-1 for the Affiliate definition.

Section 22 is the audit right; determine direction. For Vendor audits of our usage, check frequency limits, advance written notice, business-hours/remote-first conduct, confidentiality, and that Vendor bears cost absent a material underpayment. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) may hold our reciprocal assurance rights — do not flag rights that benefit us.

Look for penalties payable by Customer: late-payment interest or liquidated sums in sec-7, early-termination or shortfall penalties in sec-9, and any SLA/service-credit construct in sec-3. Service credits flowing to us are beneficial and should not be flagged; only Customer-payable liquidated damages are a deviation.

Section 19 (Warranties) is primary: check the performance/conformity warranty, its duration, and whether the remedy is real (re-performance plus refund/termination) rather than sole-remedy re-performance only. Cross-check sec-3 (Services and Performance) and sec-6 (Acceptance) for the warranty period trigger and any disclaimer in sec-19/sec-21.

Section 18 (Insurance): confirm coverage lines and limits (commercial general liability, professional/E&O, cyber given Vendor hosts Customer Data per sec-15/sec-17), plus certificate and notice-of-cancellation mechanics.

Check sec-7 (Fees) and sec-4 (Order Forms) for committed spend, minimum volumes, take-or-pay or non-reducible seat counts, and whether sec-8/sec-9 provide an exit or downward-adjustment right at renewal. Flag only if a commitment exists without a workable exit.

Section 11 (Transition Assistance and Data Return) is on point: confirm the assistance period and extension, pricing basis, return of Customer Data in a usable format on request, and deletion/certification. Cross-check sec-10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) for survival and any conditioning of data return on payment, and sec-15 for data-format obligations.
